'''Ronald William Henry Turnbull Hudson''' (16 July 1876 – 20 September 1904) was a British mathematician.<ref name=obit/>

Hudson was born into a family of mathematical talents.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=J. L. |date=1917 |title=Professor W. H. H. Hudson |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1112/plms/s2-15.1.1-w |journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=s2-15 |issue=1 |pages=lii |doi=10.1112/plms/s2-15.1.1-w|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He was the oldest of four children of William Henry Hoar Hudson, Professor of Mathematics at [[King's College London]],<ref name="obit" /> and his mother read mathematics at [[Newnham College, Cambridge|Newnham College]], Cambridge.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hilda Hudson - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Hudson/ |access-date=2024-08-05 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref> Both of his sisters became mathematicians.<ref>{{citation |last1=Barrow-Green |first1=June |title=Geometry at Cambridge, 1863–1940 |journal=Historia Mathematica |volume=33 |issue=3 |pages=315–56 |year=2006 |doi=10.1016/j.hm.2005.09.002 |last2=Gray |first2=Jeremy |author-link2=Jeremy Gray (mathematician) |doi-access=free}}</ref> 

Hudson read mathematics in [[St John's College, Cambridge]], beginning in 1895, and became [[senior wrangler]] in 1898. In the same year he was elected as a Fellow of St John's. He moved to [[University of Liverpool|University College, Liverpool]] as a lecturer in 1902, and defended a doctorate (D.Sc.) at the [[University of London]] in 1903.

In 1904, Hudson died in a mountaineering accident in Snowdonia at the age of 28.<ref name="obit">{{Citation | author=F.S.M. | title=Obituary: R. W. H. T. Hudson | jstor=3603630 | publisher=The Mathematical Association | year=1904 | journal=[[The Mathematical Gazette]] | issn=0025-5572 | volume=3 | issue=47 | pages=73–75| doi=10.1017/S0025557200241454 | doi-access=free }}</ref> 

In 1905, his posthumously-published book ''Kummer's Quartic Surface'' has gone on to become one of the most foundational texts in [[geometry]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hudson |first=R. W. H. T. (Ronald William Henry Turnbull) |url=http://archive.org/details/quarticsurface00kummrich |title=Kummer's quartic surface |date=1905 |publisher=Cambridge [Eng.] University Press |others=University of California Libraries}}</ref>
